newsitem.title: USA: Rally in U.S. Treasuries send Brady bonds soaring.
newsitem.headline: Rally in U.S. Treasuries send Brady bonds soaring.

text.p: A spectacular rally in the U.S. Treasury and stock market sent Brady bond prices soaring as market sentiment turned more positive after bond friendly data eased inflation fears, market sources said.

"The market overall seems very well bid. The numbers were quite bullish and the stock market is flying. That set the tone for the day. I dont think it is really country specific," said Marco Santamaria, vice president of emerging market research at ING Barings in New York.
The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond closed up 1-17/32 at 95.16 pushing the yield to 6.98 percent, its lowest level since March 26.
Meanwhile, the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed up 179 points to close unofficially at 6962.

The relief rally came after the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that employment costs rose 0.6 percent in the first quarter, versus market forecasts of a 0.9 percent increase. Also, durable goods orders in March posted its sharpest decline since August 1996 falling 3.0 percent.

Though today's numbers eased inflation concerns, emerging market experts said it was too early to tell what the Federal Reserve might do at its next Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on May 20.

"I think sentiment has changed somewhat. It is certainly not euphoric but from very negative it has probably changed somewhat to neutral," said Kurt Schmid, managing director of emerging market trading at SBC Warburg in New York.

"I think the bond friendly figure was the major reason for the rally but there are other important figures coming out this week, particularly the payrolls report (on Friday) and clearly that will set the tone," he added.
Other important U.S. economic reports due out include first quarter gross domestic product (GDP) and the April NAPM report on Wednesday.
Still, emerging market instruments surged on the bond friendly news, with the fixed-rate instruments outperforming the floaters.
"I think our market has followed the Treasury market with some spectacular gains," said another market source.
Emerging market debt experts said local buying by Brazilians and Argentines, coupled with short-covering also boosted the market.
For example, Argentine FRBs closed up 1/2 at 91-3/4 while the country's par bonds ended the New York trading session 1-7/8 higher at 64-7/8 bid.
Mexican Pars finished up 1-7/8 at 72-3/8 bid and the country's discount bonds closed up 7/8 at 88-3/8 bid.
Ecuador Pars rose 1-3/8 to 43-1/2 bid and its PDI bonds gained 1-7/8 to 59-7/8 bid.
Among Eastern European credits, Bulgaria FLRB were up 1-1/2 at 47-1/2 bid and Russian Vnesheconombank dollar loans were up 1-3/4 at 80-1/2 bid.
